sources.title: Introducing Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2
sources.evidence: September 11, 2026 announcement explicitly makes both models available that day via the API. Max expands the open-weight/specialized worker pool, including unspecified Nemotron models, and optimizes cost and performance. It does not disclose a Max orchestrator size, active count or neural topology.

sources.title: Sakana API model and capability documentation
sources.evidence: Maps fugu-max to fugu-max-v1.0. Max uses a fixed worker pool distinct from the configurable default Fugu pool. Documents caller-defined functions and, specifically for Max, model-invoked internal web tools with returned tool items. Provides text response and structured-text output contracts.

sources.title: Pinned official Fugu client model catalog
sources.evidence: Exact fugu-max entry gives context_window=1000000, input_modalities text/image, high/xhigh reasoning, freeform apply_patch and parallel tool calls. This is a client/service configuration, not a neural checkpoint configuration; no backbone dimensions or weights are included.

sources.title: Sakana API getting started
sources.evidence: Confirms the exact Max configuration and high/xhigh effort support; max is accepted as an alias of xhigh. Reasoning summaries are not supported for Max, which does not negate reasoning capability.

sources.title: Sakana AI API Platform Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Current API terms cover Fugu and reserve service/configuration intellectual-property rights to Sakana and its licensors, granting only limited service use. This supports proprietary hosted-service classification, not an open model-weight grant.

sources.title: Sakana Fugu Technical Report, June 23 revision
sources.evidence: Reviewed architecture/training sections and comparisons. The report covers June Fugu and Fugu-Ultra, predating September Max. It describes learned language-model orchestrators and worker pools, but does not name Max or provide its count/topology. June routing-head and Conductor implementation specifics are not automatically Max specifications.

sources.title: Testing a Gemma 4 based Fugu orchestrator
sources.evidence: August 10 research describes earlier Qwen-based orchestrators and an experimental Gemma 4 E2B replacement. It predates Max and does not identify Max as either backbone. Worker-pool models and orchestrator are separate components; experimental E2B size is not a Max parameter disclosure.

sources.title: Sakana Chat Update: Fugu Max for Everyone, Now with Memory
sources.evidence: September 17 release brings the already API-available Max orchestrator to Sakana Chat. Confirms task-dependent routing among open models and application support for image/document attachments. It supplies no new parameter or topology disclosure; application memory and attachments are not neural architecture specifications.

sources.title: Official Fugu repository inventory at pinned revision
sources.evidence: Complete nontruncated tree inspected: integration scripts, client configuration, research paper, examples and demonstrations; no Fugu Max checkpoint or neural model configuration. Repository README explicitly says its evaluations describe June models, while coordinators and pools are updated over time.

sources.title: SakanaAI public Hugging Face model inventory
sources.evidence: Official organization model inventory contained no Fugu or Fugu Max weights. Negative inventory evidence supplements the explicit API distribution, rather than proving nonexistence alone.

sources.title: Exact Fugu Max provider metadata
sources.evidence: Sakana-hosted fugu-max-20260911 endpoint advertises context1000000, text/image/file input and text output, with reasoning and tools. Its created timestamp is a provider listing, not the original launch source. File is an API container type, not evidence for a separate PDF neural modality.

name.note: Official exact variant name; current API version is fugu-max-v1.0.

developer.note: Developer and operator of the orchestrator system, distinct from the worker-model developers.

family.note: Lowercase catalog family for the Fugu orchestrator products.

release_date.note: Explicit API availability on September 11. September 17 is the later Chat rollout; original Fugu beta/GA dates do not date Max.

open_weights.note: Released as a proprietary hosted API. Open-weight workers do not constitute release of the Max orchestrator/system weights; no Max checkpoint was found in the checked official inventories.

license.note: Classification of the Max service; do not inherit licenses of worker models, research papers or example code.

parameters_b.note: No scalar total is disclosed for Max or its orchestrator. The fixed pool is not fully enumerated; summing worker counts would also misrepresent a single learned model. Earlier Trinity/Conductor counts and the Gemma experiment cannot be transferred.

active_parameters_b.note: No defined per-token active count for Max. Selecting or coordinating external worker models is not sparse-expert activation inside one neural network; the number of agents is not a parameter count.

architecture.note: Learned model orchestration is disclosed at system level. Exact Max backbone and its dense/MoE/hybrid neural topology are not. Sharing a core orchestration design with Ultra v2 does not specify a shared checkpoint or make this a neural MoE. Earlier Qwen/Gemma research does not bind Max to a particular model.

context_window.note: Exact advertised service/client limit for fugu-max. This does not establish the native training window of the undisclosed orchestrator or every worker.

modalities.note: Exact official input list and text response contract. Remove PDF as a separate neural modality: document/file acceptance is an application/API capability. These are system-level capabilities, not proof that the small orchestrator itself has a vision encoder.

reasoning.note: Official Max effort controls high/xhigh verify reasoning support; max aliases xhigh. Lack of reasoning summaries is a separate output-interface restriction.

tool_call.note: Exact Max integration enables parallel caller tools; model documentation also explains Max choosing internal web tools and returning their items. This is more than deterministic retrieval or external software simply invoking Max.

description.value: Model orchestration system that selects and coordinates a fixed pool of open-weight and specialized models for each task.
description.note: Replaces vague expert-agent wording with the documented task-dependent system and fixed worker pool; makes no unsupported benchmark superiority claim.

patch.description: Model orchestration system that selects and coordinates a fixed pool of open-weight and specialized models for each task.
patch.notes: Fugu Max (current API version fugu-max-v1.0) is a learned orchestration system with a fixed worker pool, not a disclosed single neural checkpoint. Its own total/active counts and neural topology remain undisclosed. The 1,000,000-token context and text/image input describe the public service; document/file support is not a separate neural modality. Max supports high/xhigh reasoning and model-selected tools. September 11, 2026 is API availability; September 17 is the later Sakana Chat rollout. Earlier Qwen-based Fugu research and the experimental Gemma 4 E2B orchestrator do not identify the Max backbone.

summary: Verified exact September 11 API release, one-million-token advertised service context, reasoning and tools. Added Proprietary classification, removed PDF as a neural modality and clarified the orchestrator-system description. Exact total/active counts and dense/MoE/hybrid neural topology remain undisclosed after checking original and later primary research, current docs and official public inventories. Max is a distinct optimized orchestration configuration; shared core design is not evidence of merely a billing tier.
